description: Qwen3.5-0.8B batch-1 prefill of 2048 tokens: where the Gated DeltaNet state-scan kernel comes from. TensorRT alone (the session recipe with CUDA graphs, whose scan is the hand-written Triton kernel), the best hybrid with Inductor regions, the same gdn_scan regions with a kernel written by PR 4914's KernelGenerator on the TensorRT-alone base, and the strongest Inductor configuration

notes.trt-session: The recipe the published agent session selected (not run by default). --session DIR replaces it with the recipe the session in DIR selected, and every TensorRT configuration here follows it
notes.trt-alone: TensorRT alone: the session recipe with CUDA graphs, the base of the hybrid and generated configurations; its Gated DeltaNet state scan is the hand-written Triton kernel (kernels.gdn_scan=triton-tf32) hosted in the engine
notes.trt-hybrid-attention+prologue-decay: The best hybrid of the hybrid head-to-head: trt-alone with kernels.inductor=attention+prologue-decay (Inductor regions)
notes.trt-scan-generated: trt-alone with kernels.gdn_scan=generated: the same gdn_scan regions with a kernel PR 4914's KernelGenerator writes, held to the error of the scan's FP32 products with TF32, as triton-tf32 is. Generated kernels come from the workload's kernel cache (its kernel_cache argument, else $TORCHTRT_KERNEL_CACHE, else the default directory), keyed by the region and the engine options; a build that finds none for its options generates them, so run the generated configuration once before timing it (bench_compare.py run, which has no time limit) or leave timeout_s room for the generator's 1800 s per distinct region, which it does
notes.inductor-functional-causal-tf32-fp16-fp1: The strongest Inductor configuration of the hybrid head-to-head
notes.trt-scan-loop: Not run by default: trt-alone with kernels.gdn_scan=loop, TensorRT's own kernels for the state scan
